articles.title: A tecnologia que ajuda MS a detectar focos de calor em até 10 minutos | G1
articles.standfirst: Sistema desenvolvido pelo Imasul e pela Codex monitora os 79 municípios e foi apresentado durante a COP31, na Turquia.
articles.summary: Sistema desenvolvido pelo Imasul e pela Codex monitora os 79 municípios e foi apresentado durante a COP31, na Turquia.
articles.body:
Bombeiros combatendo incêndio em vegetação na região pantaneira. — Foto: Bruno Rezende.

Tecnologia que contribuiu para reduzir em 88% o desmatamento ilegal em Mato Grosso do Sul, em três anos, foi apresentada durante a 31ª Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre Mudanças Climáticas (COP31), em Antalya, na Turquia.

O sistema integra imagens de satélite, inteligência geoespacial e análise automatizada de dados. Com isso, permite identificar áreas desmatadas com mais rapidez e tornar mais eficiente a resposta das equipes de fiscalização.

Com a tecnologia, o tempo de detecção de alertas de desmatamento caiu de 15 para cinco dias. Já a identificação de focos de calor pode ser feita em até 10 minutos.

O sistema foi desenvolvido pelo Instituto de Meio Ambiente de Mato Grosso do Sul (Imasul), em parceria com a Codex, empresa desenvolvedora de soluções baseadas em inteligência de dados.

A empresa apresentou os resultados do projeto na última sexta-feira (15), durante a COP31, como exemplo de aplicação tecnológica na implementação de políticas climáticas.

O sistema monitora 357 mil km² do território sul-mato-grossense, abrangendo os 79 municípios e os biomas Cerrado, Pantanal e Mata Atlântica. Segundo dados da empresa, houve redução da área de desmatamento ilegal nos três biomas entre 2023 e 2026.

No Cerrado, a área desmatada caiu de 15.105 para 2.633 hectares.

No Pantanal, a redução foi de 10.959 para 5.659 hectares.

Já na Mata Atlântica, o índice passou de 3.261 para 503 hectares.

Apresentação da iniciativa na COP31. — Foto: Divulgação.

A estrutura tecnológica reúne duas ferramentas.

O Monitor de Alertas de Desmatamento (Mades) permite visualizar ocorrências em mapas interativos, comparar imagens de diferentes períodos e cruzar informações com registros oficiais.

Após a validação técnica, o sistema gera relatórios eletrônicos de constatação, que podem subsidiar processos administrativos e ações de fiscalização.

Já o Monitor de Alertas de Queimadas (Maques) reúne informações sobre cicatrizes de fogo, localização e data das ocorrências, além da trajetória de propagação das chamas. Os dados são disponibilizados praticamente em tempo real e ajudam no acompanhamento e na resposta a incêndios.

De acordo com a empresa, a automação também reduziu em mais de 80% a necessidade de intervenção humana na elaboração de pareceres técnicos.

As plataformas cruzam alertas com mais de 20 bases oficiais, incluindo informações do Cadastro Ambiental Rural (CAR), registros de unidades de conservação, terras indígenas e autorizações ambientais.

articles.title: Saiba o que muda nas regras da vistoria exigida na transferência de veículos | G1
articles.standfirst: A nova resolução do Contran também cria o Sistema Integrado de Vistorias Veiculares, o Sisv. As inspeções vão passar a seguir critérios padronizados em todo o país.
articles.summary: A nova resolução do Contran também cria o Sistema Integrado de Vistorias Veiculares, o Sisv. As inspeções vão passar a seguir critérios padronizados em todo o país.
articles.body:
O Conselho Nacional de Trânsito mudou as regras da vistoria exigida na transferência de veículos.

A gerente da revendedora Dayene Ventura de Araújo trabalha em uma concessionária em Belo Horizonte e conta que dá um trabalhão o processo de transferência dos documentos:

“Nós temos que levar os veículos nas credenciadas do Detran para poder fazer a vistoria dos itens obrigatórios dos carros e depois dar entrada no processo físico nos postos de atendimento autorizados pelo Detran. No caso de revendas, demora em torno de cinco a sete dias para um documento ficar pronto”.

Agora, o Conselho Nacional de Trânsito determinou novas regras que prometem facilitar a vistoria de identificação veicular, que é exigida na transferência de propriedade. A verificação dos equipamentos obrigatórios do veículo passará a ter caráter apenas informativo. Ou seja , irregularidades que forem identificadas não vão impedir a transferência, mas vão constar no documento até que sejam solucionadas.

O Conselho Nacional de Trânsito também decidiu que quem comprar um carro, seminovo ou usado, vai poder escolher entre levar o veículo para fazer a vistoria em uma empresa credenciada pelo Detran ou pedir para fazer a vistoria onde quiser - em casa, na concessionária. Nesse caso, além da taxa oficial do serviço de vistoria, podem ser cobrados custos da equipe de vistoriadores com deslocamento.

Saiba o que muda nas regras da vistoria exigida na transferência de veículos — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Outra mudança é que não será preciso refazer inspeção no veículo se o dono do carro trocar de cidade ou de estado. A nova resolução do Contran também cria o Sistema Integrado de Vistorias Veiculares , o Sisv. As inspeções vão passar a seguir critérios padronizados em todo o país. Na venda para outro estado, um único laudo vai valer na origem e no destino do veículo.

O Ministério dos Transportes informou que a resolução não estabelece uma data para a implantação do Sisv. Depois que o sistema entrar em funcionamento, os órgãos de trânsito vão ter até 90 dias para se adaptar às novas regras.

O advogado de defesa do consumidor Júlio Moraes Oliveira acredita que as mudanças são positivas tanto para quem vende como para quem compra:

“Antes, cada Detran tinha sua regra própria e isso dificultava um pouco. Então, agora, o consumidor tem facilidade, inclusive de comprar carros por leilão na internet, eles podem comprar o carro em qualquer lugar do país e fazer a vistoria em qualquer estado porque o sistema vai ser unificado”.

articles.title: Cidades vizinhas somam 108 casos de sarna humana em MS | G1
articles.standfirst: Itaporã soma 34 casos da doença e prevê reabertura de segunda creche na quarta-feira (18); em Dourados, notificações chegam a 74.
articles.summary: Itaporã soma 34 casos da doença e prevê reabertura de segunda creche na quarta-feira (18); em Dourados, notificações chegam a 74.
articles.body:
Pais e alunos chegando no Centro Municipal de Educação Infantil (CMEI) Milton Menani, em Itaporã. — Foto: TV Morena.

As aulas no Centro Municipal de Educação Infantil (CMEI) Milton Menani, em Itaporã , foram retomadas nesta segunda-feira (16), após oito dias de suspensão devido a um surto de escabiose, conhecida como sarna humana, que atingiu crianças e servidores da unidade.

Agora, a expectativa é pela reabertura de outra unidade da cidade, o CMEI Maria Rodrigues Dias, onde também foram registrados sete casos da doença. A previsão é que as aulas sejam retomadas na quarta-feira (18).

Desde o início do surto, Itaporã já registrou 34 casos de escabiose. O problema também preocupa moradores de Dourados , município vizinho localizado a apenas 16,6 quilômetros de distância, onde já foram contabilizados 74 casos.

Nesta segunda-feira, na entrada do CMEI Milton Menani, pais e responsáveis foram recebidos por servidores em meio à preocupação com a saúde das crianças. Assim que soube da situação na unidade onde a filha estuda, a autônoma Milena Ivoniski seguiu as orientações da direção.

“Mandaram para a gente, no grupo da escola, avisando que ia ficar essa semana sem aula por conta do surto. Explicaram a prevenção, explicaram como remediar e pediram para quem tiver crianças com sintomas levá-las ao médico para iniciar o tratamento”, comentou Milena.

Apesar da retomada das atividades, a unidade terá a higienização reforçada nos próximos dias para evitar novos casos entre alunos e servidores. A diretora da creche, Bianca Lacerda, explicou que os cuidados serão mantidos durante o período de retorno.

“Nós vamos prosseguir com a higienização das salas todos os dias, a limpeza do pátio, e as crianças vão estar levando agora a toalha para essa semana que a gente está retornando, para ver como vai proceder, se vai acontecer novamente, se vai surgir novamente, para a gente ter esse momento de adaptação mais seguro para as nossas crianças”, explicou.

Em Dourados, a situação mais preocupante foi registrada no Centro de Educação Municipal Infantil Recanto Raízes, no Jardim Água Boa. Somente nesta unidade, 24 crianças e 16 servidores foram diagnosticados com a infecção.

Nesta segunda-feira (16), durante uma reunião entre a Secretaria Municipal de Saúde e representantes das escolas municipais, foram repassadas orientações sobre a identificação dos sintomas, prevenção e higienização dos ambientes. A pasta também confirmou o aumento de casos da doença na cidade.

Centro de Educação Municipal Infantil Recanto Raízes, no Jardim Água Boa, em Dourados. — Foto: TV Morena.

O CEIM Professor Bertilo Binsfeld, que até então não aparecia na relação divulgada pela prefeitura, confirmou dez casos. Já os CEIMs Recanto Raízes e Beatriz de Barros Bumlai registraram outros nove casos cada um.

O município também investiga casos suspeitos na Escola Municipal Franklin Luiz Azambuja.

Além dos registros de escabiose, a Secretaria Municipal de Educação de Dourados recebeu notificações de impetigo, uma infecção bacteriana de pele que também provoca feridas. Apesar das ocorrências, o cenário é considerado controlado, segundo o enfermeiro Fábio Hortelan, especialista da prefeitura de Dourados.

“Tanto a escabiose quanto o impetigo são doenças de prevalência, tanto para crianças quanto para adultos. Então, são doenças que a gente já espera nas populações. O que nos preocupa é se ela virar um surto, quando são registrados muitos casos num período curto de tempo”, concluiu.

articles.title: Goregaon East property prices jump 51% and West rates rise 38% as redevelopment, Metro expansion and new road projects transform Mumbai suburb from residential pocket into mixed-use hub
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Once known primarily as a residential suburb, Goregaon is gradually acquiring a new identity.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Once known primarily as a residential suburb, Goregaon is gradually acquiring a new identity. Better road and Metro connectivity, large-scale redevelopment and the growth of commercial centres are changing the way people live and work here. The suburb is increasingly emerging as a mix of residential neighbourhoods, business districts and retail destinations, say real estate experts.Redevelopment of housing societies has gathered pace in both Goregaon East and West, as a shortage of available land pushes the suburb towards urban renewal. Hundreds of societies, many housed in ageing buildings dating back to the 1960s and 1970s, are opting for redevelopment.Nikhil Bhatia, managing director and co-head of capital markets at CBRE India, said, "Large redevelopment initiatives, including MHADA's Motilal Nagar enclave, are reinforcing Goregaon's transformation."A major connectivity boost is expected from the 12.2-km Goregaon-Mulund Link Road (GMLR), which will connect the Western and Eastern Express Highways through twin tunnels beneath Sanjay Gandhi National Park. The project is expected to cut travel time between Goregaon and Mulund substantially. Another major project, the proposed Versova-Bhayander coastal road, is expected to improve north-south connectivity across the western suburbs, with a planned connector near Mindspace in Malad linking it to GMLR.Metro connectivity is expanding too. Operational Metro Line 2A connects Goregaon with Andheri, Malad, Kandivli and Dahisar. Upcoming Lines 2B and 6 are expected to improve access to BKC, Powai and the eastern suburbs, while extensions of Line 7 towards Mira-Bhayandar and the airport are planned. Together with Goregaon and Ram Mandir railway stations, these links are expected to strengthen the suburb's connectivity with different parts of Mumbai.Improved connectivity is also supporting the growth of commercial activity. Business districts and employment centres such as Mindspace, NESCO, Nirlon Knowledge Park and Film City, along with the Oshiwara Development Corridor, are helping create a mix of offices, homes, shopping and leisure destinations.Developers and property brokers say demand is being supported by connectivity, social infrastructure and proximity to employment centres. Gagan Mehta, director at AGM Vijaylaxmi Group, said, "Goregaon's appeal has widened beyond its traditional catchment areas. We are seeing interest from homebuyers in neighbouring areas such as Jogeshwari, Malad and Kandivali."Residential market data covering projects launched between Q1 2022 and Q3 2026 shows that property prices have risen substantially in both parts of Goregaon.In Goregaon East, the weighted average selling price rose from Rs 26,831 per sq ft of carpet area in 2022 to Rs 40,430 in 2026, an increase of around 51%. In Goregaon West, it went up from Rs 23,926 to Rs 32,944 during the same period, a rise of around 38%.Knight Frank's Gulam Zia said, "Goregaon's property market remained resilient even when east-west connectivity was largely limited to two flyovers and the Metro had only recently opened. Much of the planned infrastructure is still in the pipeline, but demand is likely to grow even without these projects."The two markets have also seen different patterns in new housing supply and sales. Goregaon East recorded 767 apartment launches in 2025, of which 348 had been absorbed. In Goregaon West, 1,323 apartments were launched and 899 were absorbed. In 2026, up to Q3, Goregaon East recorded 241 launches and 35 absorptions, while Goregaon West saw 1,333 launches and 424 absorptions.The figures point to a considerably larger supply pipeline in Goregaon West, where launches have also outpaced sales. In Goregaon East, the gap between launches and absorptions widened in the first nine months of 2026. Absorption refers to cumulative sales from homes launched in the respective year, as recorded in the dataset.Ram Naik, co-founder and CEO of The Guardians Real Estate Advisory, said, "Goregaon's growth is becoming increasingly differentiated across its micro-markets. The east is emerging as a stronger commercial and employment destination, while the west continues to benefit from established residential demand, retail infrastructure and redevelopment."However, the pace of redevelopment and rising population density have also raised concerns. "Construction in Goregaon has gone unchecked. There are serious questions about whether the city's urban environment can absorb further high-density development. Developers wield excessive influence, and there are insufficient checks on the construction of tall buildings," said activist Zoru Bathena.Redevelopment can help replace Goregaon's ageing housing stock, but higher population density can put considerable pressure on drainage, roads, open spaces and public amenities, said activist Anil Galgali. "Rising property prices could also make homeownership increasingly difficult for some buyers." A Mhada official said the scale of transformation requires coordinated planning. articles.title: Upset shareholders sue Intel; say that company did not share on time the disastrous …
articles.summary: Intel shareholders have sued the company, accusing it of hiding the impact of a long slowdown in PC sales that led to its stock price falling nearly 29%
articles.body: Intel shareholders have sued the company, accusing it of hiding the impact of a long slowdown in PC sales that led to its stock price falling nearly 29% in a single day, Reuters reports. The lawsuit was filed in a federal court in San Jose, California, by shareholders led by a Michigan pension fund. They claim Intel failed to disclose in time how weak PC sales and excess inventory would hurt its revenue. The shareholders also allege that Intel raised $23 billion by selling shares at $95 each in mid-August, even though the company was already halfway through what they called a “disastrous” third quarter.As stated in the Reuters report, the shareholders allege that Intel's problems with PC sales and excess inventory outweighed ⁠data center construction and other benefits related to the artificial intelligence boom.Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan disappointed by manufacturing supply shortagesIntel reported its quarterly results on October 30. The California-based company then projected lower-than-expected fourth-quarter revenue and profit. It also forecasted a prolonged slowdown in PC sales.Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan then told analysts that he was disappointed by manufacturing supply shortages, an "unprecedented memory crunch," and resulting softness in PCs. "We need to ​address these challenges ​with urgency," Tan added.Intel says budget laptop chips are already sold outDuring the earnings call, CEO Lip-Bu Tan said demand for the company’s budget-focused Wildcat Lake chips “is outstripping supply.”CFO David Zinsner confirmed that the chips are now sold out. “We've seen significant growth in Wildcat Lake. It’s coming exactly at the right time because it’s cost-optimized and we’re seeing a lot of focus in that regard,” he said.Wildcat Lake chips are appearing in lower-cost Windows laptops, including the new Dell XPS 13 and HP OmniBook 5 14. These devices are positioned as more affordable options in a market where rising memory costs have put pressure on PC prices.However, some of these laptops start with just 8GB of RAM. articles.title: IAF's long wait for Tejas Mk-1A nears end: Why it matters
articles.summary: Good news is in store for the Indian Air Force (IAF) as it is expected to induct the Tejas Mk-1A fighter aircraft this financial year, bringing an end to
articles.body: Good news is in store for the Indian Air Force (IAF) as it is expected to induct the Tejas Mk-1A fighter aircraft this financial year, bringing an end to a long wait.Deliveries of the initial batch of 83 aircraft were originally scheduled to begin in February 2024. The induction is now expected to take place before March 31, 2027.These aircraft are expected to be inducted into the No. 3 Squadron (Cobras) of the IAF. The IAF has contracted for a total of 180 aircraft of this type in two tranches, the first for 83 aircraft and the second for 97 aircraft.The delay was caused due to integration related issues, coupled with the inability of the engine manufacturer to provide powerplants in a timely manner.The IAF already has two fighter squadrons equipped with the Tejas — No. 18 Squadron (Flying Bullets) and No. 45 Squadron (Flying Daggers). This variant of the Tejas is more advanced than the earlier Initial Operational Clearance (IOC) and Final Operational Clearance (FOC) configurations. The air force had ordered 40 Tejas fighters and trainers, with many of them in service. So far, 220 Tejas aircraft have been ordered by the IAF, two of which have crashed.Speaking at an event in New Delhi, Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, who recently took over the reins of the IAF, stated, "Very shortly, we will have LCA Mark 1A joining Indian Air Force within this financial year. We will have a squadron, and then we will continue developing, and we will take it further."The Tejas currently in service and the Mk-1A share the same basic airframe and are powered by the same GE F404-IN20 engine. However, the Mk-1A incorporates improvements in avionics, sensors and electronic warfare capabilities.The Mk-1A features an Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) radar, an advanced self-protection jammer, an improved radar warning receiver, an upgraded mission computer, a digital flight-control computer and smart multifunction displays. The aircraft has also been redesigned for easier maintenance and improved serviceability. The Mk-1A is intended to provide greater situational awareness, survivability and combat effectiveness than the two preceding configurations.The development comes at a time when the IAF's fighter strength has dwindled to 29 squadrons. The Indian Air Force has a sanctioned strength of 42 fighter squadrons. Several squadrons have been number-plated (stood down) due to a lack of fighter aircraft. This is the IAF's lowest fighter squadron strength since the 1960s.Besides the Tejas Mk-1A, Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd is also working on the larger Tejas Mk-2, which will come with enhanced capabilities. India is also developing the fifth-generation Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA). IAF chief Dixit said, "We will continue developing, and we will take it further. Not only LCA Mark 1A, now LCA Mark 2 will roll out maybe next year".The Indian Air Force is also looking to procure 114 Rafale fighter aircraft, which will form six squadrons of the force. At the same time, the IAF is looking to replace as many as six squadrons of Jaguars, three squadrons of MiG-29s and three squadrons of Mirage 2000s over the next decade.

articles.title: A 74-year-old widow sent half her life savings to someone pretending to be David Attenborough; the fraudster used AI-generated images to convince her they were in a relationship
articles.summary: A Facebook message from someone claiming to be Sir David Attenborough eventually turned into a relationship that a 74-year-old Canadian widow believed
articles.body: A Facebook message from someone claiming to be Sir David Attenborough eventually turned into a relationship that a 74-year-old Canadian widow believed could lead to marriage and a new life in Britain. For six months, Diane exchanged intimate messages with the supposed broadcaster, sent him money and began making plans to leave her home behind. As reported by The Independent, the person on the other side of the screen was not Attenborough. Using fabricated photographs, an AI-generated video and a succession of personal crises, the fraudster persuaded her to part with a substantial portion of her savings. By the time her son discovered what was happening, the financial damage and emotional fallout had already begun.Fake David Attenborough Facebook account drew Diane into a six-month romance scamDiane first encountered the fake celebrity account in October 2024. The profile presented itself as belonging to Attenborough, and the initial contact soon developed into regular conversations. As reported, the person managing the account suggested moving their exchanges to Telegram, claiming the messaging platform would offer greater privacy.What followed was an increasingly consuming online relationship. Diane began staying awake late into the night to speak with the man, who said he was following British time. Their conversations became part of her daily routine, and within weeks, the two were exchanging declarations of love.There was little reason for Diane to believe that the person behind the account was facing the sort of financial difficulties he described. But the supposed relationship soon acquired a series of problems that required her help. He claimed his former wife had taken hundreds of thousands of pounds from him, leaving him struggling to recover the money.How the supposed broadcaster began asking for moneyThe requests for financial assistance started with what appeared to be a temporary problem. The fraudster told Diane that he needed money to pay a lawyer who could help retrieve the funds allegedly taken by his former wife. He also claimed he needed the money to arrange life-saving treatment for a kidney condition.Diane initially transferred CA$4,000, equivalent to approximately £2,200. The requests did not stop there. Over the following weeks, she sent further amounts, sometimes a few hundred dollars and sometimes several thousand.The payments were made through cash deposits into a cryptocurrency account specified by the fraudster. This arrangement made the transactions harder to trace and left Diane with little prospect of recovering the money once it had been transferred.By March 2025, she had handed over CA$22,000, roughly half of her life savings. She was left with only CA$6,000 in an account she could access.Diane later acknowledged that she had suspected something was wrong even while the relationship continued. There were moments when she questioned the identity of the person she was speaking to, but her feelings had become deeply involved. She knew the situation did not always make sense and continued sending money anyway.AI-generated images and a fake video helped sustain the deceptionThe fraudster also had to maintain the appearance that he was the celebrated natural historian Diane believed she was communicating with. An AI-generated photograph of Attenborough was used on the Facebook profile, giving the account a visual identity that could appear convincing to someone unfamiliar with the signs of digital impersonation.As Diane began asking more questions, the person behind the account supplied further material. Eventually, she received a pre-recorded video featuring an AI-generated version of Attenborough, complete with a fabricated voice.The technology gave the fraudster another way to reinforce the story. Rather than relying entirely on written messages and photographs, the account could now appear to offer a personal video from the man Diane believed was her partner.Her doubts did not disappear completely. She withdrew the remaining funds from the cryptocurrency account after becoming suspicious, but the break was short-lived. A few days later, the fraudster contacted her through another Facebook profile, presenting the new account as further proof of his identity. Diane resumed communicating with him.Marriage plans and the prospect of moving to LondonThe relationship had by then moved beyond requests for money to discussions about their future together. The supposed Attenborough spoke about marriage and a life in Britain, suggesting that Diane could join him in London. There was a condition attached to this plan. She would first have to sell her Canadian flat and send him the proceeds.Diane began preparing for the move and bought a passport. To her, the relationship appeared to be heading towards a permanent commitment, even though she had never met the person she believed she was going to marry.Her son Jim eventually discovered the extent of what had happened. When he confronted her at home one Sunday morning, he learnt that his mother had been communicating with someone impersonating the veteran broadcaster for six months and had already transferred a large part of her savings. The confrontation was painful. Jim believed his mother had become so involved with the fraudster that she was prepared to abandon her existing life and leave him behind.His intervention prompted Diane to distance herself from the account and begin dealing with the consequences of the deception.The fraudster tried to pull her back after she ended contactBreaking away did not immediately end the manipulation. Around ten days after Jim confronted his mother, the fraudster sent Diane an email while continuing to pose as Attenborough. The message accused her of pretending to love him and blamed her for causing him emotional pain. It was another attempt to make Diane feel responsible for the breakdown of a relationship that had never been genuine.By then, she understood that she had been defrauded. Yet the emotional attachment had not simply vanished with that realisation. The Independent reported that she still had lingering feelings for the person she had believed she loved. About six weeks after receiving the email, Diane emptied her savings account and sent the remaining money to the fraudster.The episode left her family facing not only the loss of her money but the difficulty of rebuilding trust and helping her recover from the experience. Jim and his mother subsequently opened a joint bank account for her finances, allowing him to monitor deposits and withdrawals. Diane also sought assistance from her family doctor.Romance fraud relies on relationships built over timeDiane's experience reflects a pattern seen in romance fraud cases, where financial requests emerge only after fraudsters have spent considerable time establishing emotional connections with their targets.Rather than asking for a large payment immediately, perpetrators may begin with everyday conversations, gradually introducing declarations of affection and claims of personal hardship. Once a victim feels responsible for the supposed partner's wellbeing, requests for money can become increasingly difficult to refuse.Research cited in The Independent's investigation found that romance fraud often involves repeated payments, reflecting the length of the relationships fraudsters build. The publication also referred to findings from UK Finance showing that romance scams accounted for £20.5 million in reported losses during the first half of 2025, an increase of more than a third compared with the same period in 2024.The amount lost annually to this type of fraud had also nearly doubled since 2020, according to the figures reported. Social media and messaging services have made it easier for fraudsters to approach people while concealing their actual identities. Diane's case began on Facebook before moving to Telegram, taking the conversations away from the original platform.Figures from TSB cited in the investigation indicated that 58 per cent of romance fraud cases began on social media. Celebrity impersonation featured in 29% of those cases.Fake David Attenborough pages remained active despite reports to FacebookDiane's experience also formed part of a wider investigation into how fraudulent celebrity profiles were handled by Facebook, which is owned by Meta. The Independent identified two Facebook pages pretending to represent Attenborough. Both had been active for several months and encouraged fans to contact them privately. The publication reported the accounts to Facebook, but the platform initially declined to remove either, saying its enforcement efforts prioritised cases involving the most severe potential real-world harm.The newspaper subsequently contacted the pages itself. Both responded while pretending to be the broadcaster. One account went on to engage a reporter in an attempted romance scam, following a pattern similar to the one Diane had described. Around six weeks into the exchange, the person behind it requested £2,000 through Bitcoin.The investigation also examined 100 other recently active fake celebrity pages, each with at least 1,000 followers. One had accumulated 206,000 followers. Facebook initially said that 91 of the reported pages did not breach its content policies. Five were removed, while the remaining cases received different responses. Some accounts continued attracting followers during the following months. One impersonating Denzel Washington reportedly gained more than 100,000 additional followers before Meta was contacted directly by the newspaper. Most of the remaining pages were subsequently taken down.Meta said impersonating public figures was against its policies and that it had removed or disabled the pages brought to its attention. The company also said it used automated systems and facial recognition technology to identify fraudulent accounts.For Diane, however, the damage had already been done long before the wider investigation brought attention to the fake profiles. A person she had never met had managed to convince her that she was in a relationship with one of Britain's best-known broadcasters, leaving her with a fraction of the money she had saved over her lifetime.Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available reports and information. articles.title: UN chief hopes Donald Trump-Xi-Putin meeting will lead to nuclear disarmament efforts
articles.summary: The United Nations is ready to support any efforts towards nuclear disarmament that emerge from this week's meeting between the leaders of the United
articles.body: The United Nations is ready to support any efforts towards nuclear disarmament that emerge from this week's meeting between the leaders of the United States, China and Russia, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said on Monday, while cautioning that such an outcome was not guaranteed.Speaking at a press conference in Manila, where he is attending a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean), Guterres said the UN would be willing to contribute to any denuclearisation programme agreed upon by the three countries.“If there is a denuclearisation program, we are ready to be fully engaged in that and contribute to make it a success,” he said.“This is what we would like to see. It's not yet guaranteed that we will get there,” he added.US President Donald Trump is expected to raise nuclear arms reduction efforts during his November 19 meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. The White House said last week that the issue would be on the agenda.The three leaders are scheduled to meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in Shenzhen, southern China.China calls trilateral meeting significant for global stabilityChina's Foreign Ministry described the proposed meeting as being of “groundbreaking significance”, saying it could promote world peace and stability, Reuters reported.Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Monday that it would be the first face-to-face meeting between the heads of state of China, Russia and the United States.“They will exchange views in depth on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations, which is of groundbreaking significance,” Mao told reporters in Beijing.She said the three countries had an important responsibility to work together to address global challenges and promote stability.“Stronger communication among China, Russia, and the United States, along with managing differences and stabilising relations, serves the interests of all three countries,” she added.Mao said closer communication would also meet the expectations of the international community and help stabilise the global situation and advance dialogue and cooperation. She did not disclose specific details of the meeting's agenda.Trump's push to make nuclear arms reductions a focus of the talks has drawn objections from Beijing, which has resisted direct negotiations with Washington over its nuclear programme. China has argued that the United States and Russia should discuss the issue directly because of their much larger nuclear arsenals.Guterres calls for diplomatic solution to Iran conflictGuterres also reiterated the UN's call for a diplomatic process to end the US-Israeli war against Iran, another issue Trump is expected to raise at the summit.“What we need in relation to the situation in the Middle East, and in particular in relation to Iran and the United States, is a serious diplomatic process of negotiation to end this neither peace nor war that you are living in with devastating consequences to the global economy,” the UN chief said.The UN has repeatedly advocated nuclear disarmament, warning that rising geopolitical tensions and competition among major powers have increased global nuclear risks.Trump's four-day Asia trip also includes a visit to the Philippines on Tuesday, where he is due to meet Asean leaders and attend the first meeting of the Quad grouping of the United States, India, Australia and Japan in two years.You use AI every day. articles.title: Canada PM Mark Carney sends a message to the US government; says: Canada has best auto workers in the world, and we want them fully deployed, and we are is going to move forward either way, if you do not ...
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has signalled that Canada could turn to Chinese and other international automakers if trade negotiations with the
articles.body: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has signalled that Canada could turn to Chinese and other international automakers if trade negotiations with the United States fail to preserve an integrated North American auto industry, delivering a pointed message to the Trump administration amid ongoing trade tensions. According to a report by Associated Press, speaking to reporters in Cambodia, Carney said Canada remains committed to maintaining a North American automotive market but stressed that Ottawa would pursue other opportunities if US trade policies continue to disrupt the sector. “We have the best auto workers in the world, and we want them fully deployed, full opportunity, in an integrated North American market,” Carney said. “That market has become less integrated because of U.S. trade actions.”'Canada is going to move forward either way'Carney also revealed that the negotiations with the US President Donald Trump’s administration is still a priority for Canada, but he also warned that the outcome of these talks could influence whether Ottawa seeks deeper partnerships with European, Chinese or Japanese automakers. On being asked that if there’s a possibility of Chinese investment being used as a leverage in talks with Washington, Carney dismissed the suggestion. “It’s not leverage. But action, reaction,” he said.Referring to Canada's workforce and manufacturing assets, Carney added: “If they’re not fully utilized in a North American context, that provides other opportunities. Canada is going to move forward either way.” The remarks amount to one of the clearest signals yet that Canada is preparing alternative strategies should trade talks with the US fail to protect the country's automotive industry.China discussions on agendaThe comments made by Carney came ahead of a planned meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzen later this week. It is expected that the Chinese vehicle manufacturing and investment are said to feature prominently in the discussions. Earlier this year, Canada and China reached to an agreement enabling thousands of Chinese vehicles into Canadian market at reduced tariffs. As part of the deal, Canada’s tariff on Chinese EVs was cut from 100% to 6.1%, with an initial annual import cap of 49,000 vehicles that will gradually increase over time. In return of this, China agreed to reduce the tariffs on agricultural products from Canada. Carney has earlier argued that the agreement between Canada and China could help in attracting Chinese investment and also create jobs on Canada.Any investment must include manufacturingThe Canadian prime minister stressed that any future Chinese investment would need to involve significant manufacturing operations inside Canada rather than simply assembling imported components. “It’s not just about kit cars,” Carney said. “There has to be a manufacturing aspect involved.” He said any investment would need to meet labour standards, establish manufacturing facilities and build domestic supply chains over time, including the use of Canadian critical minerals required for electric vehicle production.Auto sector caught in trade disputeThe North American auto industry is deeply integrated, with manufacturers including Ford, General Motors and Stellantis operating facilities across Canada, the US and Mexico. Vehicle parts often cross borders several times before final assembly. However, Trump's tariff policies have disrupted that system and intensified pressure on automakers to shift production to the United States.The impact has already been felt in Canada. Ottawa recently threatened legal action against Stellantis after the company moved planned Jeep Compass production from Brampton, Ontario, to Illinois and agreed to sell its idled Canadian assembly plant.Ontario Premier Doug Ford has also criticised Canada's EV agreement with China, warning that increased imports of Chinese-made vehicles could put Canadian jobs at risk and potentially undermine access to the US market.Your child uses AI every day. articles.title: 'True democracy' must return to Myanmar: UN's Guterres backs ASEAN's diplomatic push
articles.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Monday backed fresh diplomatic efforts to engage with Myanmar's post-coup government, but stressed that an end to
articles.body: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Monday backed fresh diplomatic efforts to engage with Myanmar's post-coup government, but stressed that an end to violence and human rights violations must remain a priority.Speaking at a press conference on the sidelines of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in Manila, Guterres said engaging with parties involved in a conflict should not be seen as appeasement, while calling for immediate steps to address the crisis in Myanmar."We have never opposed the idea that it is always necessary to engage with whoever is involved in a conflict," Guterres said, AFP reported.However, he underlined that "the intolerable violations of human rights in Myanmar" must end."Violence needs to stop, humanitarian access needs to be granted, and all those arbitrarily detained must be immediately released," he said.ASEAN moves towards calibrated engagementGuterres's remarks came a day after ASEAN leaders agreed to pursue a "calibrated engagement" with Myanmar through a phased and progress-based approach.Myanmar has been excluded from high-level ASEAN meetings since the military ousted Nobel Peace Prize winner Aung San Suu Kyi's elected government in a 2021 coup, triggering a civil war that the UN estimates has killed 100,000 people and displaced more than 3.5 million.The military, led by coup leader-turned-president Min Aung Hlaing, has received backing from China, India and Russia.At the ASEAN summit, Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, also called on leaders to explore further ways to address the crisis and advance the implementation of the bloc's peace plan."As we continue to see the displacement of families, the disruption of communities and the impact on the youth of Myanmar, we must ask ourselves: what more can we do for Myanmar?" articles.title: Cape Verde president Jose Maria Neves re-elected with 64% of votes, defeats first-ever woman candidate
articles.summary: Cape Verde president José Maria Neves has won a second five-year term, securing 64% of the vote and defeating five challengers, including the country's
articles.body: Cape Verde president José Maria Neves has won a second five-year term, securing 64% of the vote and defeating five challengers, including the country's first woman presidential candidate, Joana Rosa, according to provisional results.Rosa, the main opposition candidate, received 31.4% of the vote and called Neves to concede defeat. Neves described his victory as “a great victory” in a speech after the results were announced.The election was held against a backdrop of high unemployment, rising living costs and sustained emigration, with many young Cape Verdeans leaving the Atlantic island nation in search of opportunities abroad.“The president of the republic does not have a majority; the president of the republic belongs to everyone,” Neves said, seeking to underline the largely non-partisan nature of the office.Low turnout raises questionsTurnout was low, with only 31.7% of the 418,000 registered voters casting their ballots. Neves attributed the poor participation to high emigration, population movements within the country and outdated voter records. He promised a study to examine the reasons behind the low turnout.The election had drawn attention because Rosa was the first woman to contest the presidency since the country gained independence in 1975. However, the result gives Neves a second consecutive term, extending his tenure as head of state.Cape Verde is regarded as one of West Africa's more politically stable countries, with a record of peaceful transfers of power in a region that has experienced coups and disputed elections.Under its parliamentary system, the prime minister holds most executive authority and directs government policy. The president is directly elected but has a largely ceremonial role, with powers that include vetoing legislation.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 10 platoons, drones, body cams: Bangladesh on alert in Hasina's hometown amid planned return
articles.summary: Bangladesh has deployed 10 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel in key areas of Gopalganj, the hometown of ousted prime minister Sheikh
articles.body: Bangladesh has deployed 10 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel in key areas of Gopalganj, the hometown of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina. This comes amid heightened security concerns following unrest by Awami League supporters and reports of her planned return in December, the Dhaka Tribune reported on Monday.The deployment includes armoured personnel carriers (APCs), body-worn cameras and drone surveillance to monitor the situation and prevent further violence.The BGB headquarters' media department announced the deployment. It said APCs had also been positioned to deal with any untoward incidents and carry out riot control operations if required.The force has equipped the maximum possible number of deployed personnel with body-worn cameras to monitor their activities. Live footage from the ground is also being collected through drones and other devices, with the BGB headquarters' monitoring cell overseeing the security situation.The deployment has been made under the "In Aid to Civil Power" framework on the directions of the ministry of home affairs. Personnel have been stationed at key locations based on the requirements and advice of the district magistrate, the BGB said.The security build-up follows a show of force by supporters of the banned Awami League in Gopalganj on Sunday. Party activists and members of affiliated organisations took out processions carrying machetes, axes, spears, sticks and oars, according to eyewitnesses and local reports.Despite a heavy security presence, the demonstrators marched through several parts of the district town, reopened the party's district office, vandalised a police vehicle and public installations, and set fire to the July Memorial.Following the unrest, the government transferred Gopalganj's deputy commissioner and superintendent of police.The developments come amid reports of Sheikh Hasina's planned return to Bangladesh in December. articles.body: France and Britain are set to hold an international meeting in Paris on December 4 to discuss measures against Russia's shadow fleet, a network of oil tankers accused of helping Moscow bypass Western sanctions and maintain its crude exports.French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot announced the plan on Monday, during a meeting of European Union foreign ministers in Brussels. He said the conference would be organised at the request of French President Emmanuel Macron and would focus on strengthening efforts to tackle the vessels."I will host in Paris on December 4, at the request of the President of the Republic, an international conference dedicated to the fight against the Russian shadow fleet," Barrot told reporters.Western sanctions targeting Russia's energy exports have led to the use of ageing tankers that often operate outside established regulatory and safety frameworks. These vessels have allowed Moscow to continue shipping crude oil despite restrictions imposed by Western governments.The planned conference comes after European naval forces boarded a suspected Russian shadow fleet oil tanker in the Mediterranean last week. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas disclosed the operation on Sunday, highlighting the bloc's efforts to monitor and intercept vessels suspected of helping Russia circumvent sanctions.The December meeting is expected to bring renewed attention to international cooperation against the network as European governments look at ways to restrict the movement and operations of ships involved in transporting Russian oil.The announcement also reflects continued coordination between Paris and London on measures aimed at increasing economic pressure on Moscow over its war in Ukraine.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2025, French film star Gérard Depardieu was convicted of assaulting two women on a movie set and given an 18-month suspended sentence; now he has dropped his appeal and apologised to his victims
articles.summary: For decades, Gérard Depardieu had been one of the faces of French cinema, with a career spanning more than 200 films and an international reputation for
articles.body: For decades, Gérard Depardieu had been one of the faces of French cinema, with a career spanning more than 200 films and an international reputation for memorable performances. But his legacy has been increasingly marred by sexual assault allegations and courtroom battles. The 77-year-old actor has withdrawn his appeal against a conviction involving two women on a film set, accepted the court's verdict and apologized to those affected by his behavior.Depardieu abandons appeal against convictionAccording to Reuters, Gerard Depardieu formally withdrew his appeal on Monday, November 16, against his May 2025 conviction for sexually assaulting two women during the filming of Les Volets Verts (The Green Shutters) in 2021.The decision was filed shortly after the start of the scheduled appeal proceedings, effectively ending the case and making the original judgment final. The prosecution also withdrew its appeal, as did the civil parties, meaning there will be no further proceedings in the case, Le Monde and AFP states.Depardieu admitted his conviction and apologized for his behavior,a statement by Reuters and AFP clarifies. He acknowledged that his past history of sexually suggestive jokes and provocative behavior on film sets had crossed lines and hurt people, the online report states.He also apologized to anyone who may have been hurt by his actions, admitting that not wanting to hurt someone did not make the consequences of his behavior any less.Why did he get an 18 month suspended sentence?The case concerned allegations by two women who had worked with Depardieu on a 2021 film directed by Jean Becker.Among the complainants were a set decorator and an assistant director, the BBC report said. The actor was accused of inappropriate physical contact on set in Paris, including touching intimate parts of their bodies and making sexually inappropriate comments.Depardieu has denied the allegations throughout the trial. His lawyers said any contact was inadvertent or to help him keep his balance.But he was convicted by a Paris court in May 2025 and given an 18-month suspended sentence. The ruling also required him to register as a sex offender and to pay €1,000 to each of the women as compensation for further suffering arising out of the proceedings.The judge found the women’s evidence convincing and consistent, while the actor’s explanations had inconsistencies, the BBC report states.Another legal battle is aheadThe appeal process may be over, but Depardieu still has one more big legal case to contend with. Le Monde and AFP report a French investigating judge ordered him to stand trial in 2025 on allegations he raped actress Charlotte Arnould in 2018. Depardieu denies the allegations and is contesting the proceedings. So his withdrawal of the appeal in the film-set assault case does not address the separate allegations.The latest development closes a major chapter in the legal proceedings involving two women from the production of Les Volets Verts, for the time being. It’s also a milestone for a celebrated actor whose decades-long film career is now irrevocably linked to the accusations and convictions that have reshaped his public image.Images Courtesy: Wikipedia and istockYou use AI every day. articles.title: A 16th-century book with 167 paintings showing floods, blood rain and five suns was found in a German castle and sold for just over £100,000 in 2008; now it could fetch £1 million at a London auction
articles.summary: A unique 16th-century illustrated manuscript, the Book of Miracles, is set for auction in London, showcasing 167 paintings of extraordinary natural events, potentially fetching up to £1 million.
articles.body: A 16th-century illustrated manuscript featuring blood rain, five suns, devastating floods and mysterious objects in the sky could sell for up to £1 million at an auction in London on December 10.Known as the Book of Miracles, the rare volume contains 167 paintings documenting unusual natural events and apocalyptic visions. Produced in Augsburg, Germany, during the 1550s, it will be offered at Christie's with an estimated price of £700,000 to £1 million.One illustration shows five suns appearing over Leipzig in 1551, while another depicts blood rain falling over Rome in 1456. A third, dated 1552, portrays enormous hailstones striking the Dutch city of Dordrecht during a storm so severe that people feared the arrival of Judgment Day.A forgotten manuscript discovered in a German castleThe manuscript remained unknown to scholars for centuries before it was discovered in the library of a small Baroque castle in southern Germany nearly 20 years ago.It was sold in 2008 alongside the castle's furniture, carpets and other belongings for just over £100,000. Shortly afterwards, it entered the private collection of Mickey Cartin, a prominent contemporary art collector from Connecticut, The Guardian reported.The December auction will give public institutions their first opportunity to acquire the manuscript since scholars learned of its existence. Members of the public can also view it during a six-day exhibition before the sale.Despite scholarly interest, its original purpose remains unknown. It is the only known surviving copy.Paintings capture fears of the 16th centuryThe 167 illustrations record events that people of the period often interpreted as divine warnings. They include a swarm of locusts reaching Poland in 1527 during what the manuscript describes as a terrible wind, and a North Sea flood that struck the coast of Frisia in 1230, in present-day Netherlands and Germany.Other paintings depict comets, eclipses and unusual formations in the sky. An illustration showing dragons flying over Bavaria in 1533 is believed by scholars to represent the northern lights.Each painting has a German caption identifying the event, its location and the date.Eugenio Donadoni, Christie's international specialist in medieval and Renaissance manuscripts, described the volume as an exceptionally rare German wonderbook.“German wonderbooks functioned as the sensationalist mass media of their day,” Donadoni told The Guardian.He said Lutheran theologians, including Martin Luther and Philip Melanchthon, used such accounts to support their religious interpretations of the end times. However, the manuscripts also recorded reported natural phenomena through eyewitness accounts, dates and geographical details.Modern science offers explanations for some eventsSome of the unusual occurrences depicted in the book have scientific explanations. The five suns over Leipzig, for example, are thought to represent a parhelion, commonly known as a sun dog. The optical phenomenon occurs when sunlight passes through ice crystals in the atmosphere, creating bright patches that resemble additional suns.Blood rain can occur when red dust particles, often originating in the Sahara, mix with water droplets in rain clouds.“Many of these things have actual rational scientific explanations to them,” Donadoni told the outletHe compared reading the manuscript in the 1550s to following a constant stream of alarming news online, describing it as a possible 16th-century version of “doomscrolling”.The illustrations, painted in watercolour and gouache, could also attract modern art collectors because of their surreal appearance.Till-Holger Borchert, director of the Suermondt-Ludwig Museum in Aachen, Germany, who has studied the manuscript, called it “one of a kind”. He described the £1 million estimate as “very conservative”, suggesting the final price could be higher.A facsimile edition published in 2013 introduced the manuscript to a wider audience. Borchert said it had since become an icon among people interested in apocalyptic imagery.He argued that its significance extends beyond its historical record, telling newspaper: “It’s more than that. It speaks to us, to our generation.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Three UK sisters fought their brother over a £1.6 million inheritance, including £500,000 in gold kept in a safety deposit box in India; a judge ruled the valuables belonged to the family and ordered him to pay £80,000 in costs
articles.summary: Three British sisters have defeated their brother in a court battle over their late father's £1.6 million estate after a judge rejected his claims to
articles.body: Three British sisters have defeated their brother in a court battle over their late father's £1.6 million estate after a judge rejected his claims to £300,000 in cash savings and up to £500,000 in gold stored in India. Following a hearing at the Mayor's and City County Court in London, Judge Nicholas Parfitt ordered Sonny Grover to pay his three siblings' legal bills, estimated at £80,000, directly from his own share of the inheritance. According to court details reported by The Independent and The Scottish Sun, the dispute centred on the wealth left behind by 85-year-old Hari Grover, who died in September 2024 without a will. The sisters, Airan Grover-Jones, Kiran Cotterell and Kelly Puri, took legal action after accusing their brother of leaving major assets out of the official estate valuation.Disagreement over the family fortuneWhen Hari Grover died, Sonny Grover became the administrator of his estate, initially declaring its value at roughly £865,000 for probate based largely on their father's home in Ealing, west London. The three sisters challenged that valuation, arguing that the English portion of the estate alone was worth closer to £1.15 million. They maintained that their father had never intended for one child to take the lion's share of his wealth, pointing to conversations near the end of his life in which he assured them their brother would divide everything equally. During the proceedings, lawyers representing the sisters accused Sonny of having "misappropriated money and the other property" belonging to their late father.Battle over £300,000 in life savingsA major part of the trial focused on a bank account holding approximately £300,000, which the sisters identified as their father's life savings. Representing himself in court, Sonny claimed the money became his upon his father's death because he had been added as a joint account holder roughly eight years earlier. He told the court his father had visited a bank branch to sign the mandate, claimed he had deposited some of his own funds into the account and insisted bank staff told him the balance sat outside the estate.Judge Parfitt dismissed those arguments, ruling there was no proof Sonny had contributed any of his own money or held a rightful claim to the cash, especially since evidence showed Hari Grover kept the account passbook tucked away among his clothes rather than sharing access with his son. "That is indicative that the father kept this account to himself. I don't think he involved Sonny at all," Judge Parfitt said. Responding to Sonny's claim about advice from bank staff, the judge added: "It is the court, not the bank, that decides this dispute, surprisingly enough." He ruled the £300,000 formed part of Hari Grover's estate and must be shared accordingly.Gold and jewellery in an Indian safety deposit boxThe siblings also clashed over a collection of gold bars and jewellery worth up to £500,000, kept inside a safety deposit box in India. Sonny told the court his father had gifted him both the box and its contents in 2017, a claim his sisters rejected as they stated the valuables belonged to the wider family and included specific pieces meant for them. Judge Parfitt examined what Hari Grover had told his daughters before his death, noting the father had reassured them: "don't worry you can trust your brother, he will share things equally". Based on that evidence, the judge decided the father had never intended to hand over sole ownership of the collection. "I don't think it would be right to declare that the contents of the box belongs to the estate, but that Sonny and his wife held the contents on trust," Judge Parfitt ruled, ordering Sonny to produce a full record of everything inside the safety deposit box at the time he took control of it in 2017.Criticism of the brother's court conductThroughout the hearing, Judge Parfitt expressed frustration with how Sonny handled himself on the witness stand. "Sonny was an extremely poor witness because he was simply constantly argumentative," the judge said. "He is essentially seeing this case as an argument between him and his sisters and as long as he can keep swinging he is in the game." Judge Parfitt reminded him that courts rely on evidence rather than personal battles, stating: "Unfortunately that is not the way the court makes decisions. It seeks to establish what the facts are from the documents that are made available and the recollections of the witnesses." While the judge noted there was "no criticism of the work done [by Sonny] on the estate outside of the relevant items...he has done a good job", he concluded that Sonny "believes that a just result in this case is one which would see him getting everything and his sisters getting nothing, because that's what he deserves".Six months left to settle the estateDespite the sisters' request to remove their brother as administrator immediately, Judge Parfitt gave Sonny six months to finish winding up the estate under strict court conditions that forbid unilateral decisions and require notifying his sisters before taking any action. Alongside paying his sisters' £80,000 legal bill from his own inheritance share, Sonny must work with his siblings to agree on how to divide the gold in India. Addressing the four siblings directly, Judge Parfitt told them: "They need to put their big person pants on and get it sorted out."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Fifty years after Sylvester Stallone ran up the Philadelphia Museum of Art steps in Rocky, 570 people dressed as the boxer gathered at the same spot on November 13 and set a new Guinness World Record
articles.summary: Fifty years after Sylvester Stallone sprinted up the Philadelphia Museum of Art steps as Rocky Balboa, hundreds of fans returned to the same landmark in
articles.body: Fifty years after Sylvester Stallone sprinted up the Philadelphia Museum of Art steps as Rocky Balboa, hundreds of fans returned to the same landmark in matching grey tracksuits, knit caps, and black high top sneakers. On November 13, 570 people gathered at the site to attempt a Guinness World Record for the largest gathering of people dressed as the fictional boxer, according to Guinness World Records. The event was organised by Fans of Rocky and the Philadelphia Visitor Center, with support from Amazon MGM Studios, Converse, and The Rocky Run. It formed part of the city’s Rocky Season 2026 celebrations, marking five decades since the 1976 film turned a modest training sequence into one of cinema’s most recognisable images.A sea of Italian StallionsParticipants were required to follow a strict costume standard, arriving as Rocky in grey hooded sweat suits, knit caps, and black high top shoes. The result was a striking scene outside the museum, with rows of lookalikes filling the steps and preparing for the official count.Converse helped many attendees complete the look by handing out 500 pairs of Chuck Taylor high tops at the event. Stewards organised the crowd into lines as participants laughed, compared outfits, and waited for Guinness World Records adjudicator Andrew Glass to assess the attempt.When the result was announced, the crowd erupted. Guinness World Records confirmed that 570 people dressed as Rocky Balboa had set the new record for the largest gathering of people dressed as the character.The steps that became a symbolThe Philadelphia Museum of Art steps became famous through Rocky, in which Stallone’s underdog boxer trains for a title fight by running up the staircase. The scene has since become inseparable from the city’s identity, drawing visitors who recreate the climb and raise their arms at the top.Kathryn Ott Lovell, president and chief executive of the Philadelphia Visitor Center, said, as per the report on Guinness World Records' website, that the record captured the fighting spirit that Stallone showed the world through the film. She noted that while many people have run the steps over the years, the city had never seen so many grey sweat suits gathered in one place. For the organisers, the gathering was more than a costume event. It was a way to celebrate a film that has remained part of Philadelphia’s cultural identity for 50 years, while giving fans a chance to participate in a shared moment of local history.Fans travelled for the momentThe attempt drew participants from beyond Philadelphia, with Guinness World Records reporting that some attendees had travelled from Germany, England, and Hungary. Glass described the enthusiasm of the crowd as exceptional, saying he spoke with fans united by their love of the Rocky films.He also recalled speaking with one family who proudly described themselves as Rocky, with one member sporting a Rocky tattoo. The adjudicator said the event showed the power of people coming together around a film that has meant a great deal to audiences for half a century.After the official announcement, participants raced one another up the steps and cheered as shouts of “Rocky! Rocky! Rocky!” filled the area. Organisers then encouraged the crowd to continue taking part in Rocky Season events around the city.A broader Rocky celebrationThe record attempt was one part of a wider programme running from September 29 to December 3. The celebrations have included themed bus tours, the Rocky Run races and half marathon, and release events for Stallone’s new memoir, The Steps, and Amazon MGM Studios’ film I Play Rocky.The latter film, released on November 6, explores how a young Stallone brought the original Rocky to the screen. The celebrations also marked the permanent rehoming of the Rocky Statue beside the museum steps, placing the metal sculpture of the boxer with raised gloves next to the location that made him famous.The city also hosted a free outdoor Tiny Steps concert by the Philly Pops, featuring music from and inspired by the film. As attendees left the record attempt, the familiar sound of the boxer’s iconic theme added a final flourish to a day built around one of Philadelphia’s most enduring movie moments.A record with lasting meaningThe new Guinness World Record gives Philadelphia another reason to celebrate its connection to Rocky, but it also reflects the film’s unusually durable emotional appeal. Five decades on, people from different countries were willing to wait in the rain, dress in character, and gather in large numbers to honour a story about perseverance.The organisers’ celebrations are scheduled to conclude on December 3, which Philadelphia has designated as its official Rocky Day. Until then, the city has a fresh record, a crowd of 570 Italian Stallions, and another reminder that a fictional boxer’s climb up a set of museum steps can still bring people together.You use AI every day. articles.title: Defeated Bo French boasts about American heritage in an anti-immigrant rant, gets grammar-checked by Harmeet Dhillon, Dan Crenshaw: ‘Whose, not who's’
articles.summary: Republican politician Bo French, who lost the Texas Railroad Commissioner race to Democrat Jon Rosenthal, got grammar-checked on social media after he
articles.body: Republican politician Bo French, who lost the Texas Railroad Commissioner race to Democrat Jon Rosenthal, got grammar-checked on social media after he launched yet another rant against immigration, following his pre-election diatribe against South Asian students studying at Texas University. "As an American, who's family has been here for 400 years, I shouldn't have to listen to people who are in fact not from here, do not share our culture, scam our institutions, and hate our nation, because they shouldn't be here in the first place," French posted. Social media users were quick to point out the irony that despite "400 years" of heritage, he did not know the language ashe wrote "who's" in place of "whose".Former Trump official Harmeet Dhillon was one of the critics. "Whose," she wrote, referring to the grammatical error. "Also, you are an ignorant bigot whose racist rhetoric helped turn off many Americans from voting Republican in Texas. You should do the party a favor and disappear from public life. This is MY party and country as much as it is anyone’s," Dhillon, who resigned from the post of Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights, Department of Justice, after the midterm election, wrote.Congressman Dan Crenshaw also took a swipe at French, writing: "Ok well in 400 years you couldn’t learn proper English grammar…?"Other X users joined the pile-on, turning French's claim about his family's 400-year American history into a running joke. One user wrote: "You'd think that in 400 years one of you might have learned to spell 'whose'. Time to assimilate, no?" Another commented: "400 years of familiar history and their descendant is just a racist poster and failed candidate for office?"Others pointed out that French's surname itself had European origins, while some suggested he should learn English before questioning whether other people belonged in the United States.Bo French's controversial post targeting Indian students at Texas universityFrench's latest outburst comes after months of controversy over his social media remarks targeting South Asian students at the University of Texas at Austin. In September, French shared a photograph of predominantly South Asian students celebrating the University of Texas Longhorns' victory over Ohio State in a football game."I heard UT graduation this year looked like this. I didn't believe it. The problem is now obviously far worse than anyone imagined," he wrote alongside the photograph.The remarks triggered widespread criticism, including from prominent Republicans. The students who were in the photograph spoke out and clarified that they were born in the US and were Americans and that it was "insane" to be subjected to such racism from a candidate for public office.French did not take his comments back. Neither did he apologize. And this became a major issue in his campaign for Texas Railroad Commissioner election. He lost the race ending more than three decades of Republican control of the commission. Rosenthal secured approximately 52.5% of the vote against French's 45.6%.You use AI every day. articles.title: Poland detains three teens over 'terror plot' linked to neo-Nazi movement
articles.summary: Polish security services have arrested three teenagers suspected of preparing terrorist attacks, after uncovering alleged links to an international
articles.body: Polish security services have arrested three teenagers suspected of preparing terrorist attacks, after uncovering alleged links to an international neo-Nazi movement.The Internal Security Agency (ABW) arrested two 17-year-olds and a 16-year-old, Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister overseeing Poland's special services, said on Monday.The two older suspects had allegedly shared information through messaging apps about producing homemade explosives, improvised firearms and pyrotechnic materials for a planned attack. Investigators also found chemical substances at a premises used by one of the teenagers that could potentially be used to manufacture explosives.Siemoniak said the suspects had promoted Nazi and fascist ideology and had moved beyond spreading extremist views to actions that could amount to terrorism.Two suspects sent to pretrial detentionA court ordered the two 17-year-olds to remain in pretrial detention, while the 16-year-old was placed in a juvenile detention facility.The investigation is being conducted by the Regional Prosecutor's Office in Gdansk and the ABW. Prosecutors said investigators were examining the extent of the alleged preparations and trying to identify whether other people were involved.Authorities have not publicly identified the teenagers.Arrests follow deadly shootingThe arrests come days after a deadly shooting in Krakow, which has heightened concerns about extremist violence in Poland.On November 7, a gunman killed six people and injured 16 others in the city's historic main square. Preliminary findings suggested the attacker may have been influenced by far-right ideology, Polish officials said. The suspected gunman died in hospital on November 9 after being shot by police.The shooting also triggered a political dispute over the attacker's motives, with opposition nationalist politicians questioning the initial assessment.Polish security services had detained another 17-year-old in September on suspicion of preparing a mass-casualty attack targeting locations including a school and a mosque. Prosecutors said that teenager had promoted Nazi and fascist ideology and participated in an online group linked to extremist activities.Authorities have not established any connection between the September case, the latest arrests and the Krakow shooting.You use AI every day. articles.title: Third US aircraft carrier arrives in Mideast as tensions with Iran simmer
articles.summary: The US has brought three aircraft carriers into the Middle East as tensions with Iran threaten to spiral into a wider war.
articles.body: The US has brought three aircraft carriers into the Middle East as tensions with Iran threaten to spiral into a wider war. The arrival of USS Theodore Roosevelt adds thousands of troops and hundreds of combat aircraft to Washington's military presence in the region.It comes amid fresh US strikes on Iranian targets, attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Tehran's refusal to allow international nuclear inspections.The USS Theodore Roosevelt entered the US central command's (CENTCOM) area of responsibility on Sunday, November 15, according to a US official cited by Axios journalist Barak Ravid. Its arrival brings the number of American aircraft carrier strike groups in the region to three, alongside USS George HW Bush and USS George Washington.The Roosevelt had initially been expected to replace one of the carriers already deployed in the region. However, USS George Washington remained in the CENTCOM area, allowing all three carrier strike groups to operate there simultaneously, The National reported.According to The War Zone, the Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group includes the guided-missile cruiser USS Chosin and guided-missile destroyers USS Paul Hamilton and USS Decatur. The three warships provide additional air defence, missile capabilities and protection for the carrier.The three aircraft carriers significantly expand Washington's ability to conduct sustained military operations across the Middle East. Each carrier can accommodate around 60 to 75 aircraft, including F/A-18 Super Hornet fighter jets, EA-18G Growler electronic warfare aircraft and E-2D Hawkeye airborne early-warning aircraft.They are powered by nuclear reactors, allowing them to operate for extended periods without conventional refuelling.Each carrier also carries an estimated 5,000 to 6,000 personnel, including its crew and embarked air wing. Their accompanying guided-missile cruisers and destroyers add Aegis air-defence systems, Tomahawk land-attack missiles and anti-submarine warfare capabilities.Together, the three carrier strike groups provide the US Navy with hundreds of aircraft, extensive missile capabilities and the ability to launch sustained air operations without relying entirely on military bases in the region.The development comes amid a fresh escalation in the US-Iran conflict, with both sides stepping up military operations after weeks of stalled diplomatic efforts. Iran has resumed attacks on US-linked targets in the Gulf, while Washington has carried out fresh strikes on Iranian military installations.Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed that it launched six drones targeting a US air-defence radar facility at Al-Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain on Sunday. Bahrain said its air defence systems intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks. The US military had earlier denied that an Iranian strike on its radar facility caused any damage, Reuters reported.The US military subsequently launched airstrikes on Iranian missile launchers in Bandar Lengeh and Sirik in southern Iran on Sunday night, according to Euronews. The strikes followed the attacks on US-linked facilities in Bahrain and escalating threats to commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient.
