articles.title: Jeffrey Epstein did not commit suicide, was likely killed: Top forensic expert
articles.summary: A forensic expert on Monday claimed that convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein was likely killed by someone else and did not die by suicide.
articles.body: A forensic expert on Monday claimed that convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein was likely killed by someone else and did not die by suicide.Dr Michael Freeman, who reportedly spent a year going through Epstein’s complete autopsy file provided by Epstein’s brother, concluded that Epstein’s injuries “are not explained by a suicidal hanging,” according to the New York Post.He claimed that certain marks could only be accounted for by “homicidal strangulation.”Freeman presented his conclusions at the Middle Temple, a London legal society. The New York Times reported that he said the injuries on Epstein’s body point to a struggle, which contradicts the medical examiner’s findings.Freeman, who gave testimony against former Minneapolis officer Derek Chauvin at his murder trial over George Floyd’s death, pointed to what he described as “fingernail marks” above the ligature line, a bruise at the base of the neck, and a deep, fresh bleeding wound in the left shoulder muscle. In his view, all of these indicate homicide rather than suicide.“I cannot think of a scenario in which he could have caused the spectrum of injuries he has… other than if Epstein himself had wanted to stage his suicide as a homicide,” Freeman told the BBC in an interview.“I believe that the evidence is most consistent with an assault, a ligature strangulation from behind and most probably using that same ligature to suspend the body from the bunk bed.”The New York City medical examiner’s office maintains that it stands by its 2019 conclusion that Epstein took his own life in his Manhattan jail cell.Conspiracy theorists have long maintained that Epstein was murdered inside the Manhattan federal jail to silence him after his arrest on numerous charges that might have put him behind bars for decades.According to Freeman, his “new evidence” stems from details about the position of Epstein’s body when it was discovered and the point where the ligature was anchored. He argued that the injuries normally expected from a hanging in that position do not match those found on Epstein’s body.Freeman did not examine the body himself and has only viewed photographs. He nonetheless argued that he has been able to see the most critical element, the shape and nature of the ligature mark.“Looking at it in person isn’t going to look any different than looking at it in the 30 plus photographs that we have of it,” he told the BBC. “That’s not going to change anything.”Multiple investigations have found no evidence that anyone else was involved.Epstein documents made public in February showed that the New York medical examiner who supervised the autopsy initially hesitated to rule the death a suicide because of the case’s high profile nature.You use AI every day. articles.title: Mumbai's Juhu beach sees 5-fold spike in garbage after Chhath Puja
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Juhu beach saw garbage collection surge fivefold to 150 tons on Monday, a day after Chhath Puja celebrations drew thousands to the shoreline.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Juhu beach saw garbage collection surge fivefold to 150 tons on Monday, a day after Chhath Puja celebrations drew thousands to the shoreline. The figure was 120 tons above the beach's average daily collection of 30 tons over the preceding eight days. The celebrations, which draw thousands to the shoreline for rituals and prayers, leave behind large quantities of waste, including flowers, food and other ritual offerings, contributing to coastal and marine pollution if not cleared promptly.An official said cleaning operations could not begin on Sunday evening, despite staff being ready, as the beach was packed with people, leaving no room for workers or machinery. "A conservative estimate puts the crowd at no fewer than four lakh people. We saw people beginning to gather from around 3 pm on Sunday, carrying mats and other seating arrangements to secure their spots. There was simply no space to even stand, let alone deploy cleaning staff and machinery. We could therefore begin the clean-up only after sunrise on Monday, once the crowds had dispersed," the official said.The clean-up began in full swing around 8.30 am on Monday and continued into the evening, with work still underway at 6 pm. Even additional manpower and machinery could not significantly speed up the operation, given the volume of waste. "We had brought in additional workers and machinery expecting to clear the beach faster. However, the scale of the clean-up meant even these additional resources could not speed up the process as much as anticipated. articles.title: Whistleblowers wanted
articles.summary: A whistleblower is a special person.
articles.body: A whistleblower is a special person. When others keep their heads down, and go with the flow, no matter how murky it is, this individual reports wrongdoing – such as waste, fraud, abuse, corruption, or dangers to public health and safety – that would otherwise continue in darkness. This is often at great personal risk, because the wrongdoing serves powerful interests. That’s why 60 odd countries have national whistleblower laws.In India, it was the 2003 murder of Satyendra Dubey, an NHAI engineer who exposed corruption in the Golden Quadrilateral highway project, that gave momentum to The Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014. But as IFS officer Sanjeev Chaturvedi’s recent plea before the Supreme Court highlights, this Act still hasn’t been notified.Even with such a law, things wouldn’t be easy for a whistleblower. Jeffrey Wigand, who in mid 1990s blew the whistle on Brown & Williamson, then the third largest tobacco company in US, says, “You’ll never be the same.” Even the most ‘successful’ whistleblowing is not a rosy picture.Wigand himself lost both a marriage and a first-rate corporate career, and became a high school science teacher. But from US’s multiple federal laws and UK’s Public Interest Disclosure Act 1998 to EU’s groundbreaking Whistleblower Directive 2019, what nations say with such protections is how much whistleblowers matter to the health of govt, economy, and the public.GOI told Parliament last year that the 2014 legislation needs amending to safeguard “against disclosures affecting sovereignty and integrity of India, security of the State, etc”. There are other criticisms, such as how the legislation concerns itself mostly with public servants, and not the private sector, which is quite anachronistic.But even in other countries, whistleblower protections require reforming and updating. Do not let the perfect be the enemy of the good, is a valuable principle of legal pragmatism. Let whistleblowers in India have the sanctuary Parliament gave them more than a decade ago, and improvements can follow.Disclaimer: Views expressed above are the author's own.

articles.title: Prince William and Kate to attend Earthshot Prize event today in Mumbai
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Senior members of the British royal family, Prince William and Catherine, Princess of Wales, arrived in Mumbai on a two-day visit on Monday.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Senior members of the British royal family, Prince William and Catherine, Princess of Wales, arrived in Mumbai on a two-day visit on Monday. Their three-day trip to India centres around the Earthshot Prize Awards, which will be distributed in the city on Tuesday.The couple flagged off their tour with a shot at gully cricket alongside cricketer Sachin Tendulkar and schoolgirls from various foundations at Ballard Estate. They savoured sweet tea served to them in a traditional kulhad and enjoyed a ride on the Mumbai Metro train from Vidhan Bhavan to BKC. After completing their Mumbai tour, they will depart for New Delhi where a meeting is scheduled with PM Narendra Modi on Nov 18.For BMC's A Ward, the visit of the royals to Ballard Estate on Monday morning meant a last-minute civic makeover.Roads were given a thorough wash, tree beds spruced up, garbage cleared from street corners and ongoing cement-concretising works expedited to ensure the stretch was ready for the royal couple's gully cricket match. Water tankers were deployed to clean the roads while civic staff worked to restore stretches affected by ongoing road works and make them motorable.Amid the flurry of preparations, one moment came as a pleasant surprise for the municipal staff: an executive engineer from A Ward found himself sharing the cricket pitch with the royals and even took a catch during the game.BMC executive engineer Viraj Jadhav of A Ward held a catch as the princess struck the ball after Sachin Tendulkar handed her the bat. The match was held on N Morarji Marg, near War Memorial Island, with Ballard Estate's heritage architecture providing the backdrop.The choice of Ballard Estate was significant for its architectural character as well as its proximity to the docks. Developed in the early 20th century, the heritage precinct is known for its Edwardian-Neo-Classical and Renaissance-inspired buildings, which give it an old-world character reminiscent of parts of London.Atul Kumar, founder-trustee of Art Deco Mumbai, said trade flowed through the historic docks into the erstwhile Bombay.
